scope: Proposition 3.2 (Table construction) of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose the auxiliary primes (3.1) are supplied, and suppose a deterministic procedure has the following uniform contract: for every integer 1 ≤ b < n, it factors every monic polynomial of degree at most b over Fp using table entries only for primes at most b. Then the complete table through n can be built in increasing prime order. Its construction calls that procedure at most once for each odd prime q ≤ n, on a polynomial of degree q − 1; each such call uses only already constructed table entries. Apart from these factorization calls, the construction has bit cost polynomial in E, n, and log p, with an absolute exponent. Each stored odd-prime field has degree at most q − 1, and the temporary field Vq has degree at most q(q − 1) over Fp.
